runs.title: Ported task jar_lid_open: one planned move above the perceived jar, then home
runs.what: A session started from the ported task folder efe_dexhand/jar_lid_open (version 2) with run.py --task-folder: the folder's scene, start files, scene hook and instruction; depth from the scene's own four cameras and the right wrist camera. The program locates the jar from depth (one object: jar and lid are not separated), moves the open right hand to 15 cm above its top and goes home. Nothing is touched; this is not an attempt at the task. The folder's rule answers NOT_EVALUABLE because version 2 of the folder declares no sha256 of the hook file; the original checker inside the episode recorded no stage, no success and no failure. No tracking policy used; hand: scripted postures (open).
runs.prompt: Open the jam jar with the robot's right hand and set its lid aside on the worktop. Scene (world frame, metres, z up, +x forward from the robot): the worktop top is at z = 0.75 and spans |x| <= 0.45, |y| <= 0.58. A filled 297 ml glass jam jar (550 g, 67 mm body diameter, 110 mm tall, rim at z = 0.86) stands upright on the worktop centred at x = -0.22, y = -0.08. Nothing holds the jar: it stands on its own weight and glass-on-worktop friction, which resists only about 0.13 N m of twisting torque, so the hand must turn the lid without turning, sliding or tipping the jar. Its red 64.8 mm twist-off steel lid (32 g) is closed. Jar and lid are free rigid bodies. The closure is a lug thread made of contact geometry only: four inclined glass ramps on the jar neck hold four inward lugs of the lid, so the closed lid cannot be pulled off. Turning the lid counter-clockwise seen from above (positive rotation about +z relative to the jar) slides the lugs up the ramps; at 1.049 rad they pass the ramp ends, and while they sit in the gaps between the ramps (turn between 1.049 and about 1.26 rad) the lid lifts off freely; turned further without lifting, the lugs run into the next ramps' leads, and turning clockwise from the closed position tightens and jams. The lid is lightly closed: no vacuum, seal adhesion or tightening torque is modelled, and the jam is part of the jar's rigid mass, not a fluid. Complete three stages in this order. (1) Unscrew: while the lid is still seated on the thread (lid origin less than 6 mm above its closed height and within 4 mm of the jar axis, in the jar frame), its counter-clockwise turn relative to the jar, unwrapped after every physics substep, reaches at least 1.049 rad. (2) Lift clear: afterwards, the lowest point of the lid skirt rises more than 30 mm above the jar rim. (3) Set aside: afterwards, for 50 consecutive controls (1 s), the lid touches the worktop and touches neither the hand nor the jar, is upright (tilt at most 0.15 rad), has its centre at least 90 mm horizontally from the jar axis, moves at most 0.02 m/s and turns at most 0.3 rad/s, while the jar touches the worktop, is not touched by the hand, is upright within 0.10 rad and moves at most 0.02 m/s. The episode ends with success at that moment; a partial sequence never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when: the jar tilts more than 15 degrees (jar_tipped), slides more than 30 mm horizontally from its start (jar_slid) or is lifted more than 15 mm (jar_lifted); the lid touches the worktop before stage 2 (lid_knocked_off); the lid drops: while it is in the air (its lowest point more than 10 mm above the worktop top), at any substep it touches nothing (no hand, jar or worktop contact) while its centre of mass moves downward faster than 0.3 m/s (about a 5 mm free fall; there is no window to catch it again), or its centre of mass moves downward faster than 1.0 m/s whatever it touches (lid_dropped); a lid that tips over or falls flat on the worktop (lowest point within 10 mm of the worktop top) has not dropped; the jar or the lid touches the floor, its origin falls more than 5 mm below the worktop top or leaves the worktop footprint (lid_off_table, jar_off_table) or the workspace box x in [-0.45, 0.45] m, y in [-0.40, 0.40] m, z in [0.73, 1.25] m (object_left_workspace); the lid leaves the thread upward while its lugs are not in the gaps between the ramps, i.e. its turn modulo pi/2 is outside [1.019, 1.291] rad (lid_forced_through_thread); the parked left arm or the left hand touches the jar or the lid (left_arm_contact; moving the left arm is not blocked, but the task is done by the right arm and hand); or the physics becomes unstable (unstable_physics). Later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed: the joints of the Marvin right arm and its hand (the left arm stays parked with its hand open), no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct object forces. Any robot part touching the jar or the lid counts as the hand touching it. The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.

reasons: this rule declares no sha256 of the scene hook file (task.json hook.hook_sha256)
